gen_risks.description: Soaring macroeconomic inflation and global supply shocks in Sierra Leone could cause significant cost overruns for civil works and infrastructure components.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include price contingency provisions in major works contracts, conduct market pricing surveys, and monitor procurement budgets regularly.
gen_risks.evidence: macroeconomic environment, which is characterized by intensified fiscal pressures, soaring inflation driven by global supply shocks

gen_risks.description: Heavy seasonal rainfall, intense river flooding, and landslides could cause civil works suspensions, erosion, and structural damage to rural bridges and link roads under construction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-proofed technical design standards, elevate approach embankments, right-size drainage culverts, and schedule heavy foundation works during the dry season.
gen_risks.evidence: prolonged rainy season... leading to a rise in water levels in river crossings... civil works in the four sites were suspended

gen_risks.description: GoSL fiscal stress could delay or prevent the provision of committed counterpart funds ($3.1 million) needed to complete ongoing SCADeP bridge contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a legally binding counterpart contribution schedule with the Ministry of Finance and prioritize initial disbursements from Subcomponent 2b grant funds.
gen_risks.evidence: Leaves a funding gap of about US$7.1 million... Considering the current fiscal stress on the GoSL... government has committed to cover the remaining US$3.1 million

gen_risks.description: Institutional fragmentation and overlapping mandates among MTA, SLRA, SLRSA, and Traffic Police could result in poor inter-agency coordination and delayed project execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize inter-agency coordination mechanisms through the National Project Steering Committee (NPSC) and define explicit institutional roles in the Project Implementation Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: institutional framework for transport sector management in Sierra Leone is fragmented and lacks systematic coordination among the multiple agencies operating with overlapping responsibilities.

gen_risks.description: Lack of an established procurement unit and limited familiarity with World Bank procurement regulations and STEP at MTA/PCIU could cause procurement delays and non-compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified Procurement and Financial Management Specialists prior to project effectiveness, institute proper record-keeping systems, and provide continuous hands-on STEP training.
gen_risks.evidence: PCIU is yet to be established and the capacity of procurement staff in MTA is low; there is a lack of knowledge in using World Bank’s Procurement Regulations

gen_risks.description: Low internet penetration and digital literacy gaps among rural farmers, particularly women, may inhibit the widespread adoption and utilization of the upgraded AMIS mobile app.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate offline access channels such as Integrated Voice Response (IVR) systems, partner with community women's groups, and deliver tailored grassroots digital literacy training.
gen_risks.evidence: internet penetration standing at 21.2 percent... rural women and farmers often have limited access to mobile phones based on factors such as literacy rates

gen_risks.description: Informal paratransit operators (poda-podas, okadas, kekes) may resist formalization and high-capacity bus priority schemes, causing operational conflicts or service disruptions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage informal transport associations early, facilitate their integration into corporate entities (like MTC), and incorporate them into scheduled feeder bus operation contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: Public transport services are experiencing a rapid growth of unregulated informal providers... Engaging private operators including bus operators... is the key to modernize

gen_risks.description: Insufficient road maintenance funding from the Road Maintenance Fund Administration (RMFA) and ad-hoc maintenance allocation could cause rapid post-construction deterioration of road and bridge assets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize the Bridge Management System (BMS) and Road Asset Management System (RAMS) to prioritize data-driven maintenance and support national transport strategy reforms for road fund sustainability.
gen_risks.evidence: RMFA collected approximately US$12.5 million... which is a small fraction of the actual support needed for road maintenance... decision-making on road maintenance... is ad hoc

gen_risks.description: Labor influx for rural bridge and urban infrastructure civil works increases the risk of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) in local communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce worker codes of conduct, adopt a comprehensive SEA/SH Action Plan, conduct community awareness campaigns, and establish a secure, gender-sensitive grievance mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: assess the risks related to SEA/SH and prepare an SH/SEA action plan... Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment Action Plan consistent with the ESCP

gen_risks.description: Delays in fulfilling time-bound legal covenants and disbursement conditions (e.g., establishing NPSC, adopting PIM, procuring accounting software) could stall initial project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Project Preparation Advance (PPA) funding to complete draft manuals, recruit core PCIU personnel, and finalize accounting system software selection prior to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Schedule 2, Section I. A. 2(a)... Section IV, 1... Section IV, 2... Article IV 4.01.(a)... adopt and disclose updated ESMP, ESIA, RAP

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition and economic displacement along bridge approach roads, bus corridors, and market sites could trigger disputes and delay civil works commencement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and disclose Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) early, conduct transparent stakeholder consultations, and fully execute compensation prior to site handover to contractors.
gen_risks.evidence: updated Resettlement Action Plan for Component 2... potential relocation of the project-affected people and sitting of the proposed bridges and agricultural market infrastructure

gen_risks.description: Manual and unsynchronized road incident data collection across SLRSA and Police impedes effective safety monitoring and targeted traffic enforcement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finance the establishment of a centralized digital road safety database and national guidelines while delivering joint training to SLRSA and traffic police officers.
gen_risks.evidence: There is no systematic database on road safety, and Sierra Leone Road Safety Authority (SLRSA) and the police department collect road incidents manually

gen_risks.description: Heavy vehicle overloading on newly constructed long-span rural bridges and link roads could cause premature structural fatigue and shorten asset life.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design bridge structures with structural redundancy and allowance for vehicle overloads, install scour protection, and build SLRA capacity for continuous bridge lifecycle monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: The bridges will also be checked for resilience to climate change exacerbated floods, landslides, extreme temperature, and potential vehicles’ overloads.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance is rated Substantial. This project's activities are not highly sensitive to moderate perturbations in the political dispensation, although pronounced degeneration in political stability could still undermine their implementation. The more likely risk is that poor governance may affect implementation for the road sector, resulting in reduced commitment during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through close supervision, strict adherence to the criteria for beneficiary selection, and fiduciary oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed as Substantial. Sierra Leone's post-pandemic recovery was disrupted by concurrent domestic and external shocks. Inflation and exchange rate depreciation reached record levels, depressing economic activity and triggering a severe cost-of-living crisis. Fiscal accounts have deteriorated on account of macroeconomic headwinds and policy slippages, and risks to debt sustainability have intensified. The economy is projected to grow at 3.8 percent on average during 2023-2025, below the long-term trend, and this baseline is vulnerable to downside risks given recent fiscal slippages and expenditure overruns. The macroeconomic risk may raise concerns about contractors' cost overrun and delay of payment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Key macroeconomic reforms will help reduce the imbalances and avoid the downside risks. The project is 100 percent financed by IDA which will help mitigate the macroeconomic challenges to project implementation.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. The key fiduciary risks are related to the overall governance context of the project, the risk that procurement of project works may be delayed and/or result in higher-than-expected bid prices or poorly performing contractors, and difficulty retaining qualified procurement and FM professionals in the PCIU.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated by implementing an action plan that aims to strengthen the accountability and control framework for project implementation and improve overall fiduciary performance, and by ensuring adequate procurement and FM training. The PPSD will establish appropriate prequalification requirements and adopt standard lessons from experience procuring similar works contracts in Sierra Leone. The FM risk will be further mitigated by recruiting an internal auditor under PCIU.

gt_risks.description: The project's E&S risk is Substantial (para 74, explicitly pointing to section V.D for detail - para 74 states both environment risk and social risk are rated Substantial 'as indicated in section V.D'). Section V.D (paras 64-68): overall E&S risk classification is Substantial, with eight of ten Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) applying. Environmental risk is Substantial: construction activities are expected to generate air/noise nuisance, construction waste, and traffic/worker safety issues, and Component 2 in particular could affect downstream water users (water quality/hydrology, navigation, fish catch, riparian vegetation), with some impacts potentially long-term or irreversible (e.g. accidental spill of used oil/electrolytes/hazardous materials into the river during construction). Social risk is also Substantial: key risks include physical and economic displacement of boat/ferry operators, loaders, and traders after bridge construction; SEA/SH risks from the contractor workforce; elite capture in market-infrastructure interventions; social exclusion of vulnerable groups (persons with disabilities, women/small traders, the landless, elders); and secondary risks including potential child labor, communicable-disease spread from the contractor workforce, and local conflict over benefit-sharing from downstream impacts.
gt_risks.mitigation: Standard measures per the ESIA/ESMP to be prepared for project activities, including energy-efficiency measures per World Bank EHS Guidelines/GIIPs; a site-specific SEA/SH risk assessment and commensurate GBV/SEA/SH action plan; the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) and Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), disclosed April 19, 2024; hiring a social specialist with GBV/SEA/SH experience before project effectiveness; an ESIA and Resettlement Action Plan/livelihoods restoration plan already under development for the seven originally-planned bridges, with updated ESIA/ESMP/RAP and a SEA/SH action plan to be disclosed within one month of effectiveness; and a functional grievance mechanism (GM) plus Labor Management Procedures (LMP) for project workers.
